previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted due to dislodgement of his left percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube, resulting in severe flank pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging confirmed the tube was malpositioned, and it was successfully replaced via interventional radiology. Although initial urinalysis suggested infection, cultures showed no growth, and he remained afebrile, leading to discontinuation of a brief course of meropenem. His acute kidney injury, likely due to prerenal and obstructive factors, resolved with hydration and tube replacement. Pain improved with continued home analgesics. The patient expressed concerns about recurrent complications and was referred to urology for evaluation of surgical correction of his ureteral stricture. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans and continuation of suppressive fosfomycin therapy.
